The invention provides a method for measuring the connection strength between two connected measurement members.

The object to be measured includes a first measurement member and a second measurement member. Each of these measurement members is formed as a cylindrical member or a cup-shaped member. The first and second measurement members are connected to each other at their respective opening portions, so that the strength of this connection can be evaluated.

The method includes the following steps.

First, the first measurement member is fixed in place. This is done by enclosing and holding the circumferential wall of the first measurement member from the outside. At the same time, the annular end surface at the opening of the second measurement member is supported in the axial direction. In this state, the connected measurement members are positioned so that the connection between them can be subjected to a separation force.

Next, the first measurement member, which has been fixed in this manner, is held in a suspended state in midair. By suspending the fixed first measurement member, the measurement members can be arranged so that external influences caused by contact with surrounding structures are reduced.

Finally, the first measurement member is pulled in a direction away from the second measurement member. The pulling force is increased until the connection portions between the first measurement member and the second measurement member separate from each other. The force required to cause this separation is measured as the connection strength between the two measurement members.

Through these steps, the method enables the connection strength between the first and second measurement members to be measured accurately and reliably.

A method is provided for measuring the connection strength of an object formed by joining a first measurement member and a second measurement member. Each of the first and second measurement members has a cylindrical or cup-shaped form and includes an opening at one end. The two measurement members are joined together at or near their respective openings so that an annular joined portion is formed between them.

In this method, the first measurement member is fixed by holding its outer circumferential wall. The second measurement member is supported at its annular end surface, that is, at the end surface surrounding its opening. With the second measurement member supported in this manner, the first measurement member is suspended while remaining fixed by its outer circumferential wall. A pulling force is then applied to the first measurement member in a direction away from the second measurement member.

The pulling force is increased until the joined portions of the first and second measurement members separate from each other. The force required to cause this separation is measured and used as an indication of the connection strength between the two members. Because the first measurement member is held at its outer circumferential wall and the second measurement member is supported at its annular end surface, the load can be applied in a stable and reproducible manner. As a result, the connection strength of the joined object can be evaluated reliably, even when the object has a cylindrical or cup-shaped configuration.

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, yet it plays a very important role. It is called the definite article, and we use it when we are talking about something specific. For example, when we say “the book,” we usually mean a particular book that the speaker and listener both know about.

This simple word helps make communication clearer. Without “the,” many sentences would sound incomplete or confusing. It can point to a unique object, such as “the sun” or “the moon,” or it can refer to something already mentioned, like “I saw a dog. The dog was barking.”

Although “the” is short, it is one of the most common words in English. It appears in everyday conversations, books, news articles, songs, and speeches. Its importance shows that even the smallest words can have a big impact on meaning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract/claim for a method of measuring the connection strength between two cylindrical or cup-shaped members joined at their openings.
counterfactuals.output:
## Abstract

A method is provided for measuring the connection strength between a first cylindrical or cup-shaped member and a second cylindrical or cup-shaped member joined together at respective open end portions. The method includes securing one of the members in a holding fixture, engaging the other member with a loading fixture, and applying a controlled separating force between the members in a direction generally along a central axis of the joined members. The applied force is increased until relative displacement, separation, or failure of the joint occurs. A force sensor measures the force applied during the test, and a maximum measured force, or a force corresponding to a predetermined displacement or failure condition, is determined as an indication of the connection strength between the members. The method enables repeatable evaluation of the joining strength of nested, press-fit, crimped, bonded, welded, or otherwise connected cylindrical or cup-shaped components.

## Claim

1. A method of measuring a connection strength between a first member and a second member, each of the first and second members being cylindrical or cup-shaped and having an open end portion, the first and second members being joined together at their respective open end portions, the method comprising:

   positioning the joined first and second members in a test apparatus;

   retaining the first member with a first fixture;

   engaging the second member with a second fixture;

   applying, by the test apparatus, a separating load between the first fixture and the second fixture in a direction tending to separate the first and second members at the joined open end portions;

   measuring the separating load while the separating load is applied; and

   determining, from the measured separating load, a connection strength of the joined first and second members.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein the separating load is applied substantially along a longitudinal axis common to the first and second members.

3. The method of claim 1, wherein determining the connection strength comprises identifying a maximum separating load measured before separation or failure of the joined open end portions.

4. The method of claim 1, wherein determining the connection strength comprises identifying a separating load corresponding to a predetermined displacement between the first and second members.

5. The method of claim 1, further comprising measuring displacement of at least one of the first and second fixtures while the separating load is applied.

6. The method of claim 1, wherein the first fixture supports an outer surface, inner surface, rim, flange, bottom wall, or side wall of the first member.

7. The method of claim 1, wherein the second fixture engages an outer surface, inner surface, rim, flange, bottom wall, or side wall of the second member.

8. The method of claim 1, wherein the first and second members are joined by at least one of an interference fit, crimp, adhesive bond, thermal bond, weld, snap fit, friction fit, or mechanical deformation.

9. The method of claim 1, wherein the test apparatus applies the separating load at a controlled rate.

10. The method of claim 1, further comprising recording a force-displacement curve and determining the connection strength from the force-displacement curve.
